questions.q: What are the three security layers this lesson applies to the deployed endpoint?
options: Faster CPUs, more RAM, and a bigger disk
No hardcoded key, no public exposure, and screened responses
A new password, a new username, and two-factor authentication
A firewall, a VPN, and a proxy server
questions.explain: The lesson applies three layers from earlier chapters: keeping the key out of code (L16), keeping the endpoint off the public internet (L14), and screening responses if the model is user-facing (L9).

questions.q: What does DefaultAzureCredential() do that a hardcoded ClientSecretCredential does not?
options: It makes API calls faster
It disables authentication entirely
It automatically discovers and uses a managed identity, with no secret in code
It only works in local development
questions.explain: DefaultAzureCredential() picks up a managed identity automatically, so there's no client secret anywhere in the code, config file, or environment variable.

questions.q: What does the az monitor diagnostic-settings create command do?
options: Deletes an endpoint's logs permanently
Deploys a new model to the endpoint
Grants public internet access to a resource
Routes a resource's logs and metrics to a destination like a Log Analytics workspace
questions.explain: A diagnostic setting is an Azure configuration that routes a resource's logs and metrics to a destination such as Log Analytics, Event Hub, or storage.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what does disabling public network access on the resource behind the endpoint accomplish?
options: It stops the endpoint from accepting traffic from the open internet
It deletes the endpoint
It speeds up model inference
It automatically encrypts the model weights
questions.explain: Public network access controls whether a resource accepts traffic from the open internet at all — disabling it, paired with a private endpoint, keeps the service reachable only from inside your own network.

questions.q: What counts as the monitoring deliverable being complete, per this lesson?
options: A month of observed traffic with no errors
A perfect latency score under 10 milliseconds
Disabling all logging to save cost
The diagnostic setting existing and logs actually landing in the destination
questions.explain: The lesson is explicit that the deliverable is the diagnostic setting existing and logs actually flowing — not a long observation period.
